review_notes: Independently reviewed the current top-level proposal.json, not the older proposal embedded in context.prior_result. Read all 120 proposal lines, all 35 functionality lines, all 408 fact-disposition lines, and all 262 link-disposition lines.

All four proposed writes address owned subjects, use permitted fact types, and are supported by canonical source. The additional entry data-flow write correctly repairs the baseline's ordering error: x2226_b2 is cleared before ftCo_800DB368, whose executed branch sets it true.

Verified the Kirby helper definitions, actual Kirby caller, active common callback table, common mash implementation, capture-position helper, and both release routines. These establish victim-side interpretation, directional consumers, timing parameters, callback roles, and paired-release ordering without relying on rendered aliases.

The vertical helper accepts threshold equality but rejects age equality; its first successful branch takes precedence. Vertical return does not bypass horizontal processing in IASA. Writing stick age 254 is not proved to prevent acceptance under every possible configuration.

IASA's directional gate does not gate subtraction or mash processing. Common mash can perform two separate deductions, and release tests the resulting timer. No universal monotonic-countdown claim is accepted for arbitrary attributes or exceptional floating values.

CaptureCut clears the pair links before the subsequent CatchCut call, so preserving the linked pointer value is necessary. Neither that snapshot nor this review establishes independent object-lifetime ownership.

The current ledgers appropriately defer section attribution, exhaustive transition preservation, broad collision absence, and TU-level reduction/restoration claims. No additional corrective write is required for a retained fact under the specific independent dispositions below.
All 12 baseline outgoing records were compared with the link ledger. Duplicate endpoint/role records are preserved independently; no new links, entities, merges, or follow-up mutations are proposed.

Acceptance concerns the supported proposal and its explicit deferrals. It does not resolve original symbol spelling, compiled section layout, all callback exit paths, or all capture-state producer and consumer chains.
